title: Deep Learning · Chapter 1
description: Introduction to deep learning: AI and its types, machine learning basics and types, deep learning vs machine learning, and applications.

topics.title: What Is AI? Types of AI
topics.description: AI definitions, types by capability (Narrow, General, Super) and by functionality (Reactive, Limited Memory, Theory of Mind, Self-Aware).

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Artificial Intelligence (AI)?

options.text: A database that stores human knowledge
Technology that allows systems to replicate human behaviour and thoughts

questions.explanation: AI is the “mother class”: its aim is to teach computers to behave like humans, with the final goal of simulating the cognitive capabilities of the human brain.

questions.prompt: What is the final goal of AI, according to your notes?

options.text: Building models able to simulate the cognitive capabilities of human brains

questions.explanation: The final goal is models that simulate human cognitive capabilities.

questions.prompt: Types of AI by CAPABILITY (NGS) — select all that apply.

image.alt: Tree diagram of artificial intelligence branching into types based on capability and types based on functionality.

questions.explanation: Capability: Narrow, General, Super. Reactive Machines and Limited Memory are types by FUNCTIONALITY.

questions.prompt: Types of AI by FUNCTIONALITY (RLTS) — select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Functionality: Reactive Machines, Limited Memory, Theory of Mind, Self-Aware.

questions.prompt: AI that performs one specific task intelligently but fails beyond its limitations is…
questions.explanation: Narrow AI is trained only for a specific task.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of Narrow AI? (select all that apply)

options.text: A robot that thinks and adapts exactly like a human
Voice assistants like Siri and Alexa

questions.explanation: All are trained for a limited range of functions. A human-like thinking robot would be General AI.

questions.prompt: AI that can perform intellectual tasks as efficiently as humans — understanding, learning, adapting and thinking like a human — is…
questions.explanation: General AI is still a theoretical concept.

questions.prompt: General AI already exists in today's voice assistants.
questions.explanation: General AI is still theoretical. It needs self-consciousness, awareness of surroundings and independent decisions. Voice assistants are Narrow AI.

questions.prompt: AI that SURPASSES human intelligence, performs any task better than humans and understands emotions is…
questions.explanation: Super AI is an advanced version of General AI and remains hypothetical.

questions.prompt: Which is the MOST BASIC type of AI by functionality?
questions.explanation: Reactive machines work only on present data.

questions.prompt: How do Reactive Machines operate?

options.text: They store past experiences and learn from them
Only on present data, giving predetermined outputs for specific inputs; they don't store or learn from past experiences

questions.explanation: No memory, no learning from past actions.

questions.prompt: IBM's Deep Blue, which beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov, is an example of…
questions.explanation: It identified pieces and predicted moves but could not store memories or learn from past games.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, Google's AlphaGo is also an example of…
questions.explanation: Your notes list it as a reactive machine: it plays Go by pattern recognition without gaining knowledge from previous games.

questions.prompt: Which category is used MOST in modern AI applications?
questions.explanation: Limited memory systems store historical data to predict and decide, but have no long-term memory.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of Limited Memory AI? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Chatbots use recent conversation; self-driving cars use past experiences plus current road conditions.

questions.prompt: Limited Memory AI keeps a permanent long-term memory of everything it has seen.
questions.explanation: It stores past data to improve decisions but does NOT have long-term memory.

questions.prompt: AI that could understand human emotions, beliefs and intentions (still in development) is…
questions.explanation: Possible applications: collaborating robots and human–robot interaction.

questions.prompt: Which type represents the future of AI with self-consciousness similar to humans, and is far from being achieved?
questions.explanation: Self-aware systems could be fully autonomous and make moral and ethical decisions.

questions.prompt: A robot works next to factory staff and changes its behaviour when it senses a worker is stressed. This would be…
questions.explanation: Interpreting emotions and adjusting behaviour is Theory of Mind.

topics.title: Machine Learning Basics & Types
topics.description: What ML is, the ML basics (DFME), how ML works (8 steps), and supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning.

questions.prompt: What is Machine Learning?

options.text: Writing a rule by hand for every situation
A branch of AI where models and algorithms let computers learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task

questions.explanation: ML learns from data instead of hand-written rules for every task.

questions.prompt: Machine Learning is a branch of Artificial Intelligence.
questions.explanation: AI ⊃ ML ⊃ DL.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the Machine Learning basics (DFME)?

options.text: Model training → Data preprocessing → Feature selection → Model evaluation
Data preprocessing → Model training → Feature selection → Model evaluation
Data preprocessing → Feature selection → Model training → Model evaluation
Feature selection → Model evaluation → Data preprocessing → Model training

questions.explanation: DFME: Data preprocessing, Feature selection, Model training, Model evaluation.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order of how Machine Learning works?

options.text: Data collection → Problem statement → Data modeling → Data cleaning → Feature engineering → Model evaluation → Exploratory data analysis → Deployment
Data cleaning → Data collection → Problem statement → Feature engineering → Data modeling → Exploratory data analysis → Deployment → Model evaluation
Problem statement → Data collection → Data cleaning → Feature engineering → Exploratory data analysis → Data modeling → Model evaluation → Optimization & deployment
Problem statement → Data modeling → Data collection → Data cleaning → Model evaluation → Feature engineering → Exploratory data analysis → Deployment

questions.explanation: PDDFEDMO.

questions.prompt: In “How Machine Learning works”, which step comes right after Data Cleaning?
questions.explanation: … Data Collection → Data Cleaning → Feature Engineering → Exploratory Data Analysis …

questions.prompt: What is the FIRST step of how Machine Learning works?
questions.explanation: You start by defining the problem.

questions.prompt: What are the three types of Machine Learning? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement.

questions.prompt: Which type of ML trains on LABELLED data to predict or classify new, unseen data?

image.alt: Diagram of supervised learning: labelled training data is used to train a model that predicts labels for new data.

questions.explanation: Labelled = every input has the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Which type of ML finds patterns or groups in UNLABELLED data (e.g. clustering)?

image.alt: Diagram of unsupervised learning: unlabelled data is grouped into clusters by the model.

questions.explanation: Clustering and dimensionality reduction are unsupervised.

questions.prompt: Which type of ML learns by trial and error to maximise rewards?

image.alt: Diagram of reinforcement learning: an agent takes actions in an environment and receives rewards.

questions.explanation: Ideal for decision-making tasks such as games and robots.

questions.prompt: A shop groups its customers into segments using purchase history, with no labels given. Which type of ML?
questions.explanation: No labels + finding groups = clustering = unsupervised.

questions.prompt: A model learns to predict house prices from past sales that include the actual price. Which type of ML?
questions.explanation: The past sales are labelled with the correct output (price).

questions.prompt: A program learns to play a video game by getting points for good moves and penalties for bad ones. Which type of ML?
questions.explanation: Trial and error with rewards = reinforcement learning.

topics.title: What Is Deep Learning? DL vs ML
topics.description: Definition of deep learning, artificial neural networks, and how DL differs from traditional ML.

questions.prompt: Deep Learning is a subset of… (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: DL ⊂ ML ⊂ AI.

questions.prompt: What does deep learning use to learn from large datasets?
questions.explanation: Deep learning's algorithm is the artificial neural network.

questions.prompt: An artificial neural network learns high-level features from data by…

options.text: Increasing the depth (number of layers) of the network
Adding more input data columns by hand

questions.explanation: More layers → more abstract features. It also removes the need for manual feature extraction.

questions.prompt: What does “deep” refer to in deep learning?

options.text: Data stored deep in a database
The use of multiple hidden layers in the neural network

questions.explanation: Deep = many hidden layers.

questions.prompt: What is the KEY difference between traditional ML and deep learning?

image.alt: Comparison of machine learning, where a human extracts features before classification, and deep learning, where the network does feature extraction and classification together.

options.text: Traditional ML always uses neural networks
Deep learning needs a human to pick every feature
Traditional ML needs manual feature engineering; deep learning learns features automatically from raw data

questions.explanation: In ML a human expert creates features first. Deep networks learn and extract features themselves.

questions.prompt: To classify a dog photo, a traditional ML model might need features like “average pixel colour” or “edge sharpness”. Who creates these features?
questions.explanation: That is manual feature engineering.

questions.prompt: In a deep network classifying a dog photo, what do the FIRST layers typically learn?

options.text: Simple features like edges and lines
Whole shapes like eyes and ears

questions.explanation: First layers: edges/lines → middle layers: shapes like eyes and ears → final layers: “dog”.

questions.prompt: Each successive layer of a deep network learns increasingly abstract and complex features.
questions.explanation: This automatic feature learning is the main reason for deep learning's success.

questions.prompt: Which describe DEEP LEARNING (from the comparison table)? (select all that apply)

image.alt: Table comparing ML and DL: dataset size, computation needed, feature selection and accuracy.

questions.explanation: Small datasets and human feature selection describe traditional ML.

questions.prompt: Which describe traditional MACHINE LEARNING (from the comparison table)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Automatic feature learning is deep learning.

questions.prompt: You have only 200 rows of tabular data and a basic laptop. Which approach suits better, according to the table?
questions.explanation: ML works with small datasets and little computation; DL needs large data and heavy computation.

topics.title: Applications of Deep Learning
topics.description: Computer vision, NLP, speech recognition and generative AI (CNSG).

questions.prompt: What are the four application areas of deep learning in your notes (CNSG)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: CNSG.

questions.prompt: What does NLP stand for?
questions.explanation: NLP = Natural Language Processing.

questions.prompt: Which type of network excels at analysing images and videos (computer vision)?
questions.explanation: CNNs are particularly good at images.

questions.prompt: Google Photos automatically tagging faces is an example of…
questions.explanation: Identifying what is in a picture.

questions.prompt: A self-driving car locating and identifying several pedestrians and vehicles in one camera frame is…
questions.explanation: Object detection finds AND locates multiple objects.

questions.prompt: Detecting tumours from X-rays and MRIs is which computer vision application?
questions.explanation: Medical imaging detects diseases with high accuracy.

questions.prompt: Which models revolutionised how computers understand and generate human language (NLP)?
questions.explanation: Transformers power modern NLP.

questions.prompt: Google Translate is an example of…
questions.explanation: Translating between languages.

questions.prompt: Analysing customer reviews to find whether they are positive or negative is…
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis determines emotional tone.

questions.prompt: Converting spoken language into text is…
questions.explanation: Deep learning made dictation and voice assistants far more accurate.

questions.prompt: Midjourney and DALL-E creating photorealistic images from a text description is an example of…
questions.explanation: Generative AI also creates articles, poetry and code.

questions.prompt: Siri and Alexa use deep learning for which of these? (select all that apply)

options.text: Speech recognition (turning your voice into text)

questions.explanation: Voice assistants combine speech recognition with NLP.
